name: U.S. Representative from California

budget.basis: FY2025 (federal, Oct 2024 - Sep 2025) · Total federal outlays (about $7.0T), shaped by laws that Congress (House and Senate together) passes; only part is set through annual appropriations, and the rest is mandatory spending under standing law

connections.text: Elected by the People of the United States (435 seats)

targets: Speaker of the House of The House of Representatives
connections.text: Elects the Speaker of the House

constituents.basis: California 2020 apportionment population (39,576,757, which includes overseas federal personnel) divided by its 52 House seats. The Citizens Redistricting Commission's ideal congressional district population was 760,066 (39,523,437 / 52).

powers.value: The House shares legislative power with the Senate and holds the sole power to originate revenue bills and to impeach federal officials.

citations.quote: The House shares legislative power with the Senate and holds the sole power to originate revenue bills and to impeach federal officials.
It comprises 435 voting members apportioned among the states by population and elected to two-year terms, together with non-voting delegates and a resident commissioner.

notes: California has 52 of the 435 seats after the 2020 apportionment, down from 53. The 2-year term and the powers sentence are verbatim quotes from CivLab's House description (a secondary source, read 2026-11-03); verify both against U.S. Const. art. I (constitution.congress.gov, not reachable from this session). GAP: the absence of term limits (U.S. Term Limits v. Thornton, 1995) was not confirmed by any source seen, so term_limit is omitted. Salary: $174,000 since January 2009, with the 2025 rate frozen by appropriations law (CRS). I found no 2026 source. The Speaker's rate is $223,500. CONFLICT: a garbled census.gov table snippet placed 761,091 next to another state's rows; 39,576,757 / 52 = 761,091 matches California. 2026 MAP: Proposition 50 (approved Nov. 2025) replaced the CRC congressional map with a Legislature-drawn map for the 2026-2030 elections. Per Mission Local, CA-11 covers most of San Francisco, while the Excelsior, Portola, Visitacion Valley and Ingleside are in a neighboring district. I found no population figure for the Prop 50 districts. The budget figure is government-wide, not an amount a single Representative controls. CivLab's US graph (read 2026-11-03 with npm run import:civlab) describes the House as one body: 435 seats elected by the People of the United States, which elects the Speaker. It has no per-district data.
